events.text: Battle of Flodden: the English defeat the Scots, killing King James IV.
The Continental Congress officially names the new nation the United States.
The U.S. capital city is named Washington, after George Washington.
John Herschel takes the first photograph on a glass plate.
California is admitted as the 31st U.S. state.
Engineers find a moth in the Harvard Mark II computer: the first computer bug.
The Democratic People's Republic of Korea is proclaimed.
Elvis Presley makes his first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show.
Inmates take control of Attica prison in New York, beginning a four-day uprising.
Elizabeth II becomes the longest-reigning British monarch, passing Queen Victoria.

births.text: Leo Tolstoy, Russian author of War and Peace

deaths.text: William the Conqueror, King of England
